answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrate that simplification and shortening onboarding drive measurable improvements in activation and completion rates. These are the most directly relevant to the current dual decline and offer the highest probability of moving both metrics. Verification of memory_31 (signup field reduction) and memory_86 (onboarding shortening) will confirm the magnitude and durability of those lifts before committing. This approach avoids the churn risk flagged in memory_73 (40% SMB discount raised churn +12%) and doesn't require broad promotional pricing when the root issue appears to be friction rather than pricing. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for established customers but won't help the current activation problem among new/early users. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB-facing activation decline. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding has the best risk/reward profile for sustainable qualified revenue.
